newsitem.title: USA: Albright recommends Mexico certification - officials.
newsitem.headline: Albright recommends Mexico certification - officials.

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright has recommended that Mexico be recertified as a U.S. ally in the drug war, despite serious problems and congressional opposition, U.S. officials said on Friday.

Albright, after talks with President Bill Clinton, was due to announce the adminstration's decision on Mexico as part of a presentation on the annual State Department report on anti-narcotics efforts at 4:30 p.m. (2130 GMT) Friday, the department announced.
U.S. officials said they did not know for sure that Clinton had accepted Albright's recommendation.

But top White House aides have indicated that the United States would re-certify its southern neighbour as helping to fight drug trafficking, thus avoiding a cut-off in some U.S. aid, economic sanctions and a blow to Mexico's national pride.

Albright had given serious consideration to "decertifying" Mexico as punishment for a lack of anti-narcotics efforts, while also waiving any sanctions for now to give Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo time to show he is working on it, officials said.
